# City source captures

Real answers of the providers behind `apps/server/src/modules/data-platform/sources/city/`, taken
on 11/11/2026 between 01:00 and 01:13 UTC with the same generic browser `User-Agent` the platform
sends (no contact, no project name). Nothing was written by hand: a capture is either whole or cut
by whole rows, and JSON files were re-indented by Prettier.

| File                                | Downloaded (UTC) | Origin                                                                                                                                            | How it was cut                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `faa-airport-status.xml`            | 01:00:57         | `https://nasstatus.faa.gov/api/airport-status-information`                                                                                        | Whole (1,293 bytes). No program at JFK, LGA or EWR; closures elsewhere.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `nyc-dot-traffic-speeds.json`       | 01:05:21         | `https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/i4gi-tjb9.json` with `$where=data_as_of > '2026-11-10T16:06:00'`, `$order=data_as_of DESC`, `$limit=1000` | 1,000 rows (428,374 bytes) cut to 15: the newest reading of two segments with a valid reading per borough and of three with zero speed and time, plus the previous reading of segments 311 and 211. Rows whole and in their order. |
| `nyc-dot-traffic-speeds-empty.json` | 01:12:20         | The definition's own request URL                                                                                                                  | Whole: `[]`, from a replica with `Last-Modified: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 19:52:07 GMT` (another one had answered with 23:09:13 GMT at 01:05).                                                                                             |
| `nws-alerts-new-york.geojson`       | 01:04:10         | `https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active?zone=NYZ072,NYZ073,NYZ074,NYZ075,NYZ176,NYZ178`                                                            | Whole. No active alert in the five boroughs.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `nws-alerts-new-jersey.geojson`     | 01:08:18         | `https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active?area=NJ`                                                                                                   | Whole: one Frost Advisory. Taken because New York had no alert, to test a real one.                                                                                                                                                |
| `nws-hourly-forecast.geojson`       | 01:04:28         | `https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/OKX/34,44/forecast/hourly?units=si`                                                                           | 156 hours (162,566 bytes) cut to the first 24; the rest of the document unchanged.                                                                                                                                                 |

The traffic capture's `$select` also asked for `status` and `link_id`. The definition no longer
does: NYC DOT's metadata calls `status` an artifact and `link_id` repeats `id`. The reader ignores
both.
